metadata.description: Invoice field mappings, calculations and coding conventions

mappings.mapping: account.move.amount_untaxed (Taxable base or amount without VAT)
account.move where move_type IN ('out_invoice','out_refund') AND payment_state IN ('not_paid','partial') AND state='posted'
ALWAYS use invoice_date for invoice emission date. Field 'date' is the accounting entry date, NOT the invoice date.

conventions.convention: Unless the user explicitly requests 'detalle' or 'desglose por factura', ALWAYS aggregate by partner_id. Show per customer: name, count of invoices, sum(amount_residual) as total pending. Never show one row per invoice when the user asks for a customer list or summary.

To assess customer payment risk: count invoices with payment_state='paid' in last 24 months for that partner. Good payer (green): paid_count >= 3 AND paid_ratio >= 70%. Bad payer / risk (red): paid_count less than 3 OR paid_ratio less than 70%. NEVER use total invoiced amount as proxy for payment behavior. NEVER use 'amount_total_signed' for historical payment analysis — it includes unpaid invoices.
To calculate payment history: search account.move with payment_state='paid' AND partner_id=X. Do NOT search all invoices without payment_state filter — that includes unpaid invoices.

Required columns for unpaid invoice reports (unless user asks for less detail). Use EXACTLY these dictionary key names (translate to user_lang if not es_ES): - 'Cliente' → customer name - 'NIF' → partner.vat (empty string if None) - 'Facturas Pend.' → count of pending invoices - 'Importe Pend.' → sum(amount_residual) - 'Hist. Pagado' → sum(amount_total) of paid invoices in last 24 calendar months - 'Ratio Pago %' → paid_count / (paid_count + pending_count) * 100, rounded 2 decimals - Risk color: green (_row_color='#e6f4ea') if ratio>=70% AND paid_count>=3, else red (_row_color='#fdecea')
24 calendar months cutoff: date(today.year - 2, today.month, 1) NEVER use timedelta(days=730) — calendar months give consistent results across years.

ALL accounting periods are NATURAL CALENDAR PERIODS, never rolling-day approximations.
QUARTER (Q1-Q4) — last completed quarter before today: if month <= 3: Q4 prev year → (year-1, 10, 1) to (year-1, 12, 31) elif month <= 6: Q1 → (year, 1, 1) to (year, 3, 31) elif month <= 9: Q2 → (year, 4, 1) to (year, 6, 30) else: Q3 → (year, 7, 1) to (year, 9, 30) NEVER use timedelta(days=90).
HALF-YEAR (H1/H2) — last completed half-year: if month <= 6: H2 prev year → (year-1, 7, 1) to (year-1, 12, 31) else: H1 → (year, 1, 1) to (year, 6, 30) NEVER use timedelta(days=180).
FISCAL YEAR — last completed calendar year: (year-1, 1, 1) to (year-1, 12, 31) NEVER use timedelta(days=365).
MONTH — last completed calendar month: first_day = date(year, month-1, 1) if month > 1 else date(year-1, 12, 1) last_day = date(year, month, 1) - timedelta(days=1) NEVER use timedelta(days=30).
YTD (year to date): (year, 1, 1) to date.today()
REFERENCE DATE: all "last period" calculations use date.today() by default. If the user specifies a date, replace today with that date in all calculations. Example: "last quarter before 2024-06-15" → use date(2024, 6, 15) as reference.
NEXT / FUTURE PERIODS (use current date as reference, not last completed): Next quarter: from the START of the current ongoing quarter → end of next. Next half-year: from the START of the current half → end of next. Next year: (year+1, 1, 1) to (year+1, 12, 31). Current quarter (in progress): the quarter that contains today. Current half-year (in progress): the half-year that contains today.
